title: A 1-of-2 multisig fails the majority rule that governs changes to it
content:
**Side A — the live configuration.** Several Prime Relayer Multisigs are documented at a **1-of-2** signing requirement, holding full `RELAYER_ROLE`.

**Side B — the modification rule.** The clause permitting changes to those multisigs allows them only where "at least a majority of signers are required to execute transactions." A majority of two is two, so a 1-of-2 configuration does not satisfy the constraint that governs its own modification.

The practical effect is that a multisig presented as a two-party control is operationally a **single key** — either signer acts alone. The majority rule appears to be exactly the safeguard intended to prevent that, so the current state is either a grandfathered exception or an oversight.

The same shape recurs elsewhere: a 2-of-5 Core Operator multisig against a rule requiring two-thirds, and freezer sets where one organization holds a majority of seats against a lower threshold.

**To resolve:** confirm whether existing configurations were intended to be exempt from the majority constraint, or whether they should be raised to satisfy it.
